storySection.title: A Unified Brand Story in a Box
paragraphs: Perfetti is beloved worldwide for its snack range. Yet, despite their many individual hits, one thing remained elusive: bundling their products into a unified, year-round offering. They wanted a box that would do more than sell — a box that would delight, surprise, and feel like a gift no matter when you bought it. That’s where the Goodyz Box concept was born.
This wasn’t about a seasonal pack or a festive special — it needed to become an evergreen icon on the shelf. To accomplish that, Perfetti turned to Prakria for bold thinking and flawless execution.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: Perfetti faced a gap in how to present its broad product portfolio as a cohesive, gift-friendly offering.

list.text: Although Perfetti sold many individual products successfully, they “could never organize them in a single coherent space, and sell them as a consolidated box.”
The brand wanted a solution that wasn’t just seasonal, but evergreen, something that worked all year, not just during festivals.
They needed the new boxed offering to out-compete established players, while staying relevant to their target audience.
It needed to feel like a premium gifting product (design, finishing) yet be broad in appeal and versatile.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: From brainstorming to sketches, the idea crystallized around the word “goodies” : evocative, playful, full of promise. The Goodyz Box would be an assortment, a surprise bundle of favorite Perfetti products, wrapped in art and elegance.

list.title: Brand Packaging Design
list.description: The box had to feel premium without losing brand personality.

list.title: Creative Package Design
list.description: The visuals evoke the excitement of discovery, the anticipation of unwrapping.

list.title: Package Label Design & Finishes
list.description: Gold embossing, custom fonts, and artistic touches elevated the perception.

list.title: Retail Packaging Design
list.description: It needed shelf presence, not subtle, but confident, calling for attention.

list.title: Packaging Design Services
list.description: From concept to production, every step is managed for quality.

list.title: A Packaging Story
list.description: This was a product box that told a story, not just of flavors, but of generosity and celebration.

list.title: Research & Positioning
list.description: We studied gifting categories and premium boxes to see what works. We wanted this box to sit naturally in gifting aisles but also hold ground on snack shelves.

list.title: Concept & Design Development
list.description: We drafted multiple creative directions. Some leaned minimalist, others more ornamental. But the final design struck balance: bold yet tasteful, playful yet premium.

list.title: Material & Finish Selection
list.description: We chose sturdy board stock, soft-touch coatings, selective embossing, and foil accents, giving tactile delight and shelf durability.

list.title: Structural Engineering
list.description: The box structure had to hold multiple snack products securely. Our structural designers modeled internal trays and partitions so that everything sat perfectly, even with transit.

list.title: Brand Consistency
list.description: Logos, color tones, iconography, and typography all harmonized with Perfetti’s brand identity. The box never felt like a divergence from their overall brand language.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: When Goodyz Box launched, it didn’t just sell, it wowed.It became a go-to gift option all year, not just during festivals.

list.text: Shoppers responded positively to the premium look and the surprise element.
The box’s presence on shelves elevated Perfetti’s portfolio, it didn’t just sit among snacks; it stood out.
It reinforced Perfetti’s commitment to experience, not just product.
Clients and customers alike recognized that this was more than a snack packaging, it was a brand moment.

storySection.title: Redefining a Beloved Classic
paragraphs: Munch has always been a playful, mass-market chocolate wafer brand loved across India. But Nestlé saw a new opportunity — to evolve Munch into a more premium, indulgent variant: Munch Max.

The challenge was ambitious: how do you transform a familiar favorite into a premium hero without losing its core identity? How do you craft branding and marketing that appeals to loyal fans and excites new audiences craving something 'extra'?

That’s where Prakria, a top creative agency and trusted branding consultant, stepped in. With expertise in brand building, brand strategy, and creative logo design, we helped Munch Max carve out a bold new identity.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: MUNCH was a familiar, mass-market chocolate bar, but when the time came to launch a bold, premium “chunky bar” version under the name MUNCH MAX, things needed to shift.

list.text: MUNCH had long been positioned as a mass-brand, so moving into the premium category posed a brand perception risk.
The product needed to signal “premium” in a clear, immediate way, through name, design, and format, rather than simply being a variant.
It had to solidify its market position and break through into the premium segment while retaining core brand equity.
The packaging, identity and naming all needed to align around the product’s “max” size/impact to justify the premium positioning.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: We identified a clear gap,  Munch Max needed to feel bolder and richer, yet stay true to the playful energy of Munch.

list.title: Brand Creation
list.description: The name “Munch Max” was crafted to be short, punchy, and clear. Max captured the promise of more chocolate, more texture, more indulgence and a simple, powerful statement of intent.

list.title: Visual Identity
list.description: The “X” became the hero, a dynamic smash mark symbolizing intensity and energy, anchoring all brand communication.

list.title: Design Extension
list.description: Across packaging, retail, and campaign visuals, the design expressed a premium yet playful identity, merging storytelling with striking visual impact.

list.title: Outcome
list.description: A bold, cohesive brand that redefined Munch for a new generation  max in taste, max in attitude.

list.title: Brand Strategy
list.description: We established Munch Max as a sub-premium brand under Munch, employing robust motifs and powerful typography to convey a change in experience.

list.title: Logo Design Services
list.description: The "X" took center stage of the logo, transforming a letter into a unique, memorable icon of "extra."

list.title: Brand Communication & Strategy
list.description: Campaigns revolved around the idea of “max” — more indulgence, more punch, more fun. This ensured that messaging was consistent across retail, digital, and outdoor.

list.title: Creative Logo Design Services
list.description: The mark was created with flexibility in mind, flowing effortlessly across single bars, multipacks, shelf units, and digital assets.

list.title: Brand Promotion
list.description: With powerful visual language, we provided breakaway visibility in crowded shopping environments and compelling storytelling on the web.

list.title: Brand Building
list.description: Beyond just visuals, we crafted an emotional story around Munch Max — making it feel like a bold evolution of a beloved favorite rather than a detached product line.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: The Munch Max launch stood out in multiple ways:

list.text: Consumers noticed the difference. The bold “X” identity made packs instantly recognizable on shelves.
Younger audiences connected with the edgier, more indulgent tone.
Loyal Munch fans appreciated the premium upgrade without losing the original brand’s charm.
Retailers reported stronger visibility and brand recall, noting that Munch Max stood out from competitors like KitKat and Cadbury.
On digital platforms, the visual language became instantly shareable, supporting organic buzz and brand promotion.
The branding and marketing strategy didn’t just elevate the product, it re-energized the entire Munch portfolio.

challenge.title: THE CHALLENGE
challenge.description: Palmolive tried to break through the clutter of the overcrowded personal-care category by positioning itself as more than just another bath product, but a sensory experience.

list.text: The bathing-products department was crowded, with lots of brands slightly varying their body-washes and hand-washes, and making it difficult for anyone to stand out.
Palmolive was looking to transition from being seen as simply “products” to a “total bathing experience.”
The challenge was to develop an entire brand (not packaging alone) that could seize attention, offer a premium perception, and create an emotional connection.
In essence, it was about transporting Palmolive into a world of indulgence and sensory pleasure, making the ritual of bathing a special getaway rather than a daily routine.

startageySection.title: THE STRATEGY
startageySection.description: We explored bathing rituals across cultures, uncovering that bathing isn’t just cleansing, it’s delight, reflection, and escape. This insight led to the creation of “Bathing Treasures of the World”, a brand idea that elevated Palmolive from functional care to a sensory experience.

list.title: Creative Concept
list.description: The first expression of this platform was “European Bathing Secrets”, a range inspired by the luxurious elegance of Europe, seamlessly fitting within Palmolive’s global portfolio.

list.title: Design Execution
list.description: The packaging captured European refinement through elegant motifs, soft textures, and a sophisticated color palette, all balanced with Palmolive’s familiar brand assets to feel both timeless and new.

list.title: Outcome
list.description: The result was packaging that went beyond form—a gateway to sensory exploration, transforming everyday bathing into a moment of calm, beauty, and indulgence.

list.title: Brand Communication & Strategy
list.description: Every message reinforced the idea that you’re getting more than a product, you’re entering a sensorial world. We built storytelling arcs for campaigns, social media, and packaging copy around “traveling through scent, touch, and ritual.”

list.title: Logo Design / Identity Adaptation
list.description: While Palmolive’s master brand remains intact, we provided subtle visual treatments so that each variant feels like part of a curated collection unified yet distinct.

list.title: Brand Promotion
list.description: On e-commerce portals, the “Bathing Treasures” identity was used in hero banners, immersive images, and storytelling modules. Offline, we supported eye-catching point-of-sale displays and gift kits.

list.title: Creative Design Agency Role
list.description: We delivered the full scope, from concept to execution ensuring that brand building companies could rely on us for consistency, depth, and emotional resonance.

resultSection.title: The Result
resultSection.description: Palmolive’s 'Bathing Treasures' campaign transformed perception, built engagement, and created a new narrative of indulgence.

list.text: The “Bathing Treasures” narrative elevated Palmolive’s perception, giving it more premium air, especially among consumers seeking indulgence.
The European Bathing Secrets variant became a standout in e-commerce listings: beautiful visuals, storytelling, and design drew higher engagement.
The identity allowed for future expansions — more “treasure” themes from other geographies under one cohesive system.
The project reinforced that best branding is not only about surface appeal, but about building layered experiences.

whySection.title: WHY THIS MATTERS
whySection.description: Palmolive’s transformation reminds us that even a mature brand can rediscover magic through brand building, brand strategy, and creative marketing agency thinking.Branding consultants guided the vision from insight to execution.

list.text: Logo design services served the larger narrative rather than dominating it.
Brand communication & strategy tied sensory stories to real product benefits.
